Ogre Chambers 2222 is a fast-paced bullet hell indie roguelike! In the game you control a spaceship, with which you have to destroy ogres. The game is a sequel to Ogre Chambers DX which was actually a remastered version of the first game Ogre Chambers available on Gx Games. There is a variety of different ogres which all shoot at you in different patterns. You can also upograde your spaceship with different upgrades like "+10% Firerate" or "+1 Bullet" if you're lucky. If you unlock a spaceship, you can choose a different one, but remember, all spaceship have their own gimmicks! Also a new addition in this series is a gun. Now, of course there was a gun before, after all how were you meant to progress in the first game? But, in this game you can wield 2 whole guns! But that's not all, you can also CUSTOMIZE the second gun! Yes, you heard that right, CUSTOMIZE!!! The customization posibilities are CRAZY, although so you wont have the game 100%ed in the first 2 hours, customization is always randomised, just like upgrades! Overall, the game is great for its price! It just launched and its first 2 weeks after launch it will be on a sale with whole -20% off! Also, the developer is a really nice person and is always active on the games Discord server, so join it if you want to submit any bugs or ask any questions)

Disclaimer: Not a bad game, just wasn't what I thought I was buying. Might be your perfect game! I really wanted to like this game but what I understood from the description/videos was off from the actual gameplay. If you're looking for a game with crafting style customization like Noita (Steam recs this from things like Hades, Noita, Binding of Isaac) this might not be it. It's not bad at all, I just can't recommend it if you're looking for what I thought I was buying. If you're looking for quick runs with light incremental gains & RNG weapons each run you might love this! Worth noting, the core gameplay mechanics look like they differ from the demo/EA videos folks made from 2025! It looks like the crazier gameplay footage was tuned down since then, but maybe not? Either way, I didn't realize until after I bought it what was different. Mechanics spoilers ahead, but in case it's helpful for others: The upgrades are typical "pick 1 of 3" in roguelites, some are notably better than others, but standard fare (attack speed, damage, range, projectile speed, and rarely I got +1 projectile). Feels good when you get the good ones, a bit mediocre when you get the less effective ones at the rate you get them compared to combat. The customization aspect feels more like pulling a slot machine and praying for a helpful outcome. It also does not affect your "primary" weapon, only your secondary, and uses consumable ammo you get refills for. Your secondary has multiple 'slots' and each one is randomly chosen when you start. Whenever you fire it, it cycles through each slot to use that type of projectile. Each time you get to 'customize' it will pick some of those random slots and you can overwrite them with what is now being offered or you can skip, all or nothing. You don't get to pick what to overwrite & what to keep, or even if you want all of the slots or only some to get overwritten. Overall, still a super impressive game especially for a solo dev! Art style is great, music is fun. I'd like to see the description/videos edited to clarify the lack of agency you have over the gun core modifications (it seemed like I'd at least be able to pick & choose what slots I wanted to modify) and how some of the promotional footage appears to be quite high level (the sides are all cropped so you can't see how many upgrades are needed for that type of gameplay) to prevent other accidental stray reviews just from misunderstood purchases!

I discovered the game through the developer's Instagram account. I started following them after the game's release, and as I downloaded more and more, I became increasingly impressed with the developer until I finally decided to buy it. I discussed it with a friend, figuring that, worst case scenario, it would just stay in the family library for my friends (who usually enjoy these kinds of games) to play. From my first match, which didn't last long due to my lack of skill, I loved the game. It's easy to play, entertaining, and very intuitive. The colors are bright and easy on the eyes, and it has excellent replayability, boosted by the daily high score feature. Its small file size, replayability, and all these features make it very unlikely that I'll delete it when I need space or forget about it. Definitely a good purchase, a good game from a good developer.

The game is in essence a fun and engaging roguelike with unique controls that provide a decent learning curve, if you are looking for a challenge there is the option of the hardcore gamemode and trying to get hit as little as possible which is "end-game" my biggest issue is the sometimes lacking agency in decisions i.E. the gun module system being completely randomized. The game provides about 15 hours of content while a singular run usually takes 20-30 minutes if you are looking for in-depth building the game might not provide what you are looking for but it is still extremely fun to try and come up with interesting builds and adjusting them to the RNG. I'd recommend this game for people who enjoy fast paced action and decently challenging gameplay.
